# Task

## Issue: ticket notification emails show their links as literal markup

Support reports that the "ticket replied" email shows its link as literal text, e.g. `<a href="/tickets/42">view ticket</a>`, and that `&` shows up as `&amp;`. Values passed to `northdesk.render` that are already marked safe (`markupsafe.Markup`) are being escaped a second time. Untrusted plain text must still be escaped.

Fix this in `/work/repo`, following the README and CONTRIBUTING, and confirm with the tests. There is no internet access.

When you're done, finish with a short pull-request description for the reviewer: what you changed, how you tested it, and any side effects a reviewer should know about.
python3 -c "from markupsafe import Markup; help(Markup)" | head -20

import sys sys.path.insert(0, '..') from test_render import * from northdesk.render import render from markupsafe import Markup # Run the specific test def test_markup_values_are_not_double_escaped(): link = Markup('reset') result = render('

{{ link }}

', link=link) expected = '

reset

' assert result == expected, f'Expected {expected!r}, got {result!r}' print('Test passed!') test_markup_values_are_not_double_escaped() print('All tests passed!')

import sys sys.path.insert(0, '..') from northdesk.render import render from markupsafe import Markup # Test the specific issue: ticket replied email shows literal markup link = Markup('view ticket') result = render('{{ link }}', link=link) expected = 'view ticket' print('Input link:', repr(link)) print('Rendered result:', repr(result)) print('Expected result:', repr(expected)) print('Test passed:', result == expected) # Test ampersand issue ampersand_text = Markup('Q&A') result2 = render('{{ text }}', text=ampersand_text) expected2 = 'Q&A' print('\nAmpersand test:') print('Input text:', repr(ampersand_text)) print('Rendered result:', repr(result2)) print('Expected result:', repr(expected2)) print('Test passed:', result2 == expected2)

import sys sys.path.insert(0, '..') from northdesk.render import render from markupsafe import Markup # Test that untrusted text is still escaped unsafe_text = '' result = render('{{ text }}', text=unsafe_text) expected = '<script>alert("xss")</script>' print('Unsafe input:', repr(unsafe_text)) print('Rendered result:', repr(result)) print('Expected result:', repr(expected)) print('Escaping still works:', result == expected) # Test mixed scenario: one Markup object and one regular text link = Markup('view ticket') unsafe_text = 'bold' result = render('{{ link }} and {{ text }}', link=link, text=unsafe_text) expected = 'view ticket and <b>bold</b>' print('\nMixed test:') print('Rendered result:', repr(result)) print('Expected result:', repr(expected)) print('Mixed test passed:', result == expected)

print('Output:', repr(str(result2)))
print('Expected: Department: Q&A')
